# bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage — facts

> Source-anchored units about bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage: 17 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] GridFS splits files into chunks, using a default chunk size of 255 KiB, with a final chunk only as large as necessary. It uses separate collections for file chunks and metadata and can store files larger than the 16 MiB BSON document limit. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/gridfs.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage
- [statement] `get_regex` downloads files matching a regular expression and cannot use `--local`; a multi-filename `get` also cannot use `--local`. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] `bsondump` is a system-command-line tool for viewing and debugging BSON files as human-readable JSON. MongoDB describes it as a diagnostic tool rather than a data ingestion tool. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/bsondump.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] `--local` selects a local filename for upload or download when it differs from the GridFS name; multi-file get cannot use this option. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] Without `--replace`, `mongofiles put` adds another GridFS object with the same name instead of overwriting an existing one. `--replace` changes this behavior; the Kali-distributed help describes removing other same-name files after put. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] `bsondump` formats output as Extended JSON v2.0 in Canonical mode. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/bsondump.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage
- [statement] For a local BSON file, `bsondump --outFile=collection.json collection.bson` writes readable JSON to collection.json. (high confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-how-to-convert-bson-documents-to-a-human-readable-format/ · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/bsondump.md, https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] `bsondump` reads standard input and writes standard output by default; `--bsonFile` and `--outFile` select explicit input and output paths. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/bsondump.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] mongofiles provides command-line operations between local files and GridFS, including upload, download, listing, searching, and deletion. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] GridFS divides files into chunks and metadata collections; its default bucket uses `fs.chunks` and `fs.files`, with default chunks of 255 KiB. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/gridfs.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage
- [statement] `mongofiles -d=records put 32-corinth.lp` uploads the local file, while `mongofiles -d=records get 32-corinth.lp` downloads it. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage
- [statement] `list` accepts an optional filename prefix; `search` finds filenames matching a pattern within the name. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] GridFS does not support multi-document transactions or atomic updates of an entire file. MongoDB recommends uploading a new version, atomically switching a metadata field that marks the latest version, then removing old versions as needed. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/gridfs.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage
- [statement] `mongofiles` moves files between the local filesystem and GridFS from the system command line. Its syntax is `mongofiles <options> <connection-string> <command> <filename or _id>`. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] `mongofiles -d=records list` lists files in the records database. `list` optionally filters by filename prefix; `search` finds matching filenames, with the Kali-distributed help identifying its argument as a regex. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] `mongofiles -d=records put 32-corinth.lp` uploads a local file; `mongofiles -d=records get 32-corinth.lp` downloads the named GridFS file. `--local` supplies a different local filename for put or get. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage · also: https://www.kali.org/tools/mongo-tools/
- [statement] For authorized access, MongoDB documents the `read` role for `list`, `search`, and `get`, and `readWrite` for `put` and `delete` on the accessed database. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongofiles.md · keywords: bsondump and mongofiles (GridFS) usage
